newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder says sees fy 97 earnings up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder says sees fy 97 earnings up 20 pct.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc said Tuesday it expects full year earnings excluding one-time gains to rise 20 percent, as the company spends less on newsprint and advertising revenues rise.

"For April, advertising revenue is well ahead of last year, with all three categories showing gains. While we expect some increase in the cost of newsprint going forward, we still anticipate that for the year as a whole we will spend approximately 15 percent less on it than we did in 1996," said chief financial officer Ross Jones.

"The combination, along with an ever-strengthening Detroit, leaves us confident that earnings for the year -- despite dilution from the Disney acquisition and excluding one-time gains -- will be up at least 20 percent," he said.
Excluding a one-time gain, Knight-Ridder Inc earned $0.49 in the first quarter of 1997, up $0.25, or 104.2 percent, from $0.24 in the same period last year.

Including a net after-tax gain of $1.36 per share on the sale of Knight-Ridder's interest in all but one of the jointly owned cable investments it had made with Tele-Communications Inc, it earned $1.85 per share.
Knight-Ridder agreed in April to buy the Kansas City Star and three other newspapers owned by Walt Disney Co division ABC of $1.65 billion.
Knight-Ridder said in the quarter overall advertising revenue was up 7.0 percent, with retail up 6.2 percent after growing less than two percent in each of the past two years.
Business information revenue was lower because of the absence of Knight-Ridder Financial, the company said.

Knight-Ridder Information revenue fell modestly below expectations due primarily to two factors: the strong dollar in 1997, which affected revenues from European operations in the currency translation, and the deterioration of CompuServe Corp as a strong vendor for its products.
Knight-Ridder also said Tuesday it expects to launch two new products for the World-Wide Web, DialogWeb and Dialogselect. "Each is expected to have a sharply positive impact on revenues," said Jones.
